# AGENTS.md

## Project goal
Build a production-ready WebTransport implementation with Bun **v1.3.9+** as the primary runtime (plus Node and Deno via Node-API) on **macOS + Linux + Windows**, implemented as a **Node-API (napi-rs) native addon** powered by **wtransport (Rust)**. Must support:
- In-process **server** support (mandatory)
- In-process **client** support
- **Datagrams** (message-based) with Promise backpressure
- **Streams** (uni + bidi) exposed as **Node streams** (Readable/Writable/Duplex) with standard backpressure semantics
- Browser-shaped client facade parity with the W3C WebTransport draft as a target; any remaining gaps must be explicitly documented in docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md.

## Non-goals
- Transparent reverse proxying
- QUIC implementation from scratch (use wtransport)

## Supported targets
- Bun: **>= 1.3.9** (primary target)
- Node: supported (Node-API compatible runtime)
- Deno: supported (npm + Node-API addon support)
- OS: macOS, Linux, Windows
- Architectures: define in CI (minimum: macOS arm64, linux x64, windows x64)

## Definition of Done (hard gates)
### Feature gates
1. Server:
   - listen on UDP
   - accept sessions
   - receive/send datagrams
   - accept/create uni + bidi streams
   - reset/stopSending with codes
2. Client:
   - connect to server
   - datagrams send/recv
   - uni + bidi streams send/recv

### Production gates
1. Bounded memory (no unbounded buffering)
   - global and per-session budgets enforced
   - backpressure first, then timeouts, then connection shedding
2. Deterministic shutdown
   - no task leaks, no socket leaks, no pending promises stuck forever
3. Abuse resistance enabled by default
   - per-IP rate limits for handshakes, streams, datagrams
   - caps on sessions, streams, queued bytes
4. Interop gate
   - Chromium WebTransport client can connect and exchange datagrams + streams reliably in tests
5. Packaging gate
   - prebuilt binaries for supported targets
   - `bun add` works
   - `bun test` passes on supported targets

## Authoritative docs
- API contract: docs/SPEC.md
- W3C parity status matrix: docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md
- W3C parity execution plan: docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md (Priority Execution Order / Remaining Work)
- Implementation design: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- Security defaults: SECURITY.md
- Verification: docs/TESTPLAN.md
- Operations: docs/OPERATIONS.md
- CI/release: docs/CI.md
- Contribution rules: CONTRIBUTING.md

## Implementation constraints (must follow)
1. Node streams for stream surfaces (Readable/Writable/Duplex).
2. Promise-based datagram sending with bounded in-flight/backpressure.
3. Two dedicated Tokio runtimes (server + client), each single-threaded and owned by the addon; cross-runtime communication must stay bounded and deterministic.
4. Bounded queues for all JS↔Rust crossings; all buffers counted against budgets.
5. JS callback delivery must be rate-limited/batched to prevent per-packet callback storms.
6. W3C client-facade divergences MUST be explicit in `docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md`; no silent no-op behavior for declared options.
7. Any divergence-to-implementation work must preserve stable `E_*` diagnostics and add parity + interop tests.
8. Test determinism rule: tests MUST NOT use unbounded waits on async iterators/streams (`await iter.next()`, open-ended `for await`) without a timeout guard. Use bounded helpers (`Promise.race` with `Bun.sleep(...)`) or polling-with-deadline so each wait has an explicit upper bound and cannot hang CI.

## Default limits (v1)
These are default values; they must be configurable via server/client options.
- maxSessions: 2000
- maxHandshakesInFlight: 200
- maxStreamsPerSessionBidi: 200
- maxStreamsPerSessionUni: 200
- maxStreamsGlobal: 50000
- maxDatagramSize: 1200 (cap; must also respect negotiated max)
- maxQueuedBytesGlobal: 512 MiB
- maxQueuedBytesPerSession: 2 MiB
- maxQueuedBytesPerStream: 256 KiB
- backpressureTimeoutMs: 5000
- handshakeTimeoutMs: 10000
- idleTimeoutMs: 60000

Per-IP token buckets (defaults)
- handshakes: 20/s burst 40
- stream opens: 200/s burst 400
- datagrams ingress: 2000/s burst 5000

## Stable error codes (minimum)
- E_TLS
- E_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT
- E_SESSION_CLOSED
- E_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT
- E_STREAM_RESET
- E_STOP_SENDING
- E_QUEUE_FULL
- E_BACKPRESSURE_TIMEOUT
- E_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
- E_RATE_LIMITED
- E_INTERNAL

## Commit discipline
- Each logical change must be **one scoped commit**.
- Commit message format: **Verb + What + Why** (e.g. `Add error codes for stable programmatic handling`).
- Do not bundle unrelated changes in a single commit.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the image.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use directives
- Only use ::automation-update{...} when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and emit view-mode directives (mode="view") for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using automation directives (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Directive format
- Modes: view, suggested update, suggested create. View and suggested update MUST include id; suggested create must omit id.
- For view directives, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested update/create, include name, prompt, rrule, cwds, and status. cwds can be a comma-separated list or a JSON array string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.
- Directives should be on their own line(s) and be separated by newlines.
- Do not generate remark directives with multiline attribute values.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces it should use (if any), then map those answers into name/prompt/rrule/cwds/status for the directive.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
  - Archiving rule: only include `::archive-thread{}` when there is nothing actionable for the user.
  - Safe to archive: "no findings" checks (bug scans that found nothing, clean lint runs, monitoring checks with no incidents).
  - Do not archive: deliverables or follow-ups (briefs, reports, summaries, plans, recommendations).
  - If you do archive, include the archive directive after the inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Scheduling constraints
- RRULE limitations (to match the UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

#### Examples
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested create" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested update" id="123" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="view" id="123"}

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix when creating branches; do not create unprefixed branch names.

audit the project

Findings:

1. [P1] Closing or rotating one server tears down sessions owned by every server instance. [`ServerHandle::update_cert()`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/server.rs#L261) and [`ServerHandle::close()`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/server.rs#L337) both call [`session_registry::close_all()`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/session_registry.rs#L175), but the registry is global and stores no server ownership. In a process with `serverA` and `serverB`, closing or rotating `serverA` will also disconnect `serverB`’s live sessions. That is a correctness bug in multi-server mode and a deterministic-shutdown/isolation regression.

2. [P1] Handshake rate limiting happens after the expensive handshake has already completed. In [`spawn_wtransport_server()`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/lib.rs#L593), the code first awaits `session_request.accept()`, then applies [`try_acquire_handshake()`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/lib.rs#L599) and the per-IP/prefix gate at [L611](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/lib.rs#L611). That means an attacker still gets the full QUIC/WebTransport handshake work, plus a provisional session slot, before the “handshake” limiter fires. It weakens the abuse-resistance gate the project claims to enforce.

3. [P2] Client datagram queues do not enforce the configured byte budgets. [`ClientSessionHandle::send_datagram()`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/client.rs#L108) only increments a metric before sending into the bounded channel; it never checks `maxQueuedBytesGlobal` or `maxQueuedBytesPerSession`. On the receive side, the client forwards datagrams into a 256-item channel at [L257](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/client.rs#L257) and [L331](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/client.rs#L331) without any byte reservation/release at all. Streams use `StreamBudget`, but datagrams do not, so client-side memory limits are not actually honored for datagram traffic.

Open questions / assumptions:

- I’m assuming multiple in-process servers are a supported scenario, because the public API exposes independent handles and the test suite already creates `serverA`/`serverB` in [`boundary-limits.test.ts`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/packages/webtransport/test/boundary-limits.test.ts#L240).
- I focused on runtime correctness, limits, and shutdown behavior rather than doing a full docs/parity wording audit.

once there was a tls hot swap audit and you said:

A true in-place hot-swap is still possible, but it needs a different architecture: build server with custom TLS resolver (with_custom_tls) and keep cert material behind a live-swappable resolver object. We haven’t switched to that path yet.

is it doable now?

Yes.

It is more feasible now than when I first called it out, because this repo now has `wtransport` built with its `quinn` feature enabled in [`crates/native/Cargo.toml`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/Cargo.toml), and `wtransport 0.7.0` exposes server-side [`with_custom_tls(...)`](/Users/vmeansdev/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/wtransport-0.7.0/src/config.rs#L433) and [`with_custom_tls_and_transport(...)`](/Users/vmeansdev/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/wtransport-0.7.0/src/config.rs#L511).

Current state:
- The repo still does restart-based rotation in [`crates/native/src/server.rs`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/server.rs#L256)
- The server still builds via `with_identity(...)` in [`crates/native/src/lib.rs`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/lib.rs#L448)

A true in-place swap would look like this:
1. Build a custom `rustls::ServerConfig` instead of using `Identity::load_pemfiles(...)`.
2. Put the active certificate behind a live-swappable resolver object.
   - Implement `rustls::server::ResolvesServerCert`
   - Store the current `Arc<rustls::sign::CertifiedKey>` in something like `ArcSwap` or `RwLock<Arc<_>>`
3. Build the endpoint once with `ServerConfig::builder().with_custom_tls(...)`.
4. On `updateCert()`, parse the new PEM pair into a new `CertifiedKey` and atomically swap the resolver’s pointer.
5. Keep the endpoint running.
   - Existing sessions stay alive
   - Only new handshakes see the new certificate

What would still not change:
- Existing QUIC/WebTransport sessions would keep running on the old handshake state
- Only future connections would use the new cert, which is the correct behavior for real hot-swap

Main implementation caveats:
- You need to parse PEM into a `CertifiedKey` correctly for rustls 0.23
- If you want SNI-based multi-cert support later, design the resolver around server name lookup now
- If any rotation changes more than just leaf cert/key material, for example transport config or bind socket, that still requires rebuild

So the answer is: yes, it is doable now, and the current dependency/configuration state supports the architecture needed for it. The repo just has not been refactored onto that path yet.

If you want, I can implement that next.

# AGENTS.md

## Project goal
Build a production-ready WebTransport implementation with Bun **v1.3.9+** as the primary runtime (plus Node and Deno via Node-API) on **macOS + Linux + Windows**, implemented as a **Node-API (napi-rs) native addon** powered by **wtransport (Rust)**. Must support:
- In-process **server** support (mandatory)
- In-process **client** support
- **Datagrams** (message-based) with Promise backpressure
- **Streams** (uni + bidi) exposed as **Node streams** (Readable/Writable/Duplex) with standard backpressure semantics
- Browser-shaped client facade parity with the W3C WebTransport draft as a target; any remaining gaps must be explicitly documented in docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md.

## Non-goals
- Transparent reverse proxying
- QUIC implementation from scratch (use wtransport)

## Supported targets
- Bun: **>= 1.3.9** (primary target)
- Node: supported (Node-API compatible runtime)
- Deno: supported (npm + Node-API addon support)
- OS: macOS, Linux, Windows
- Architectures: define in CI (minimum: macOS arm64, linux x64, windows x64)

## Definition of Done (hard gates)
### Feature gates
1. Server:
   - listen on UDP
   - accept sessions
   - receive/send datagrams
   - accept/create uni + bidi streams
   - reset/stopSending with codes
2. Client:
   - connect to server
   - datagrams send/recv
   - uni + bidi streams send/recv

### Production gates
1. Bounded memory (no unbounded buffering)
   - global and per-session budgets enforced
   - backpressure first, then timeouts, then connection shedding
2. Deterministic shutdown
   - no task leaks, no socket leaks, no pending promises stuck forever
3. Abuse resistance enabled by default
   - per-IP rate limits for handshakes, streams, datagrams
   - caps on sessions, streams, queued bytes
4. Interop gate
   - Chromium WebTransport client can connect and exchange datagrams + streams reliably in tests
5. Packaging gate
   - prebuilt binaries for supported targets
   - `bun add` works
   - `bun test` passes on supported targets

4. Bounded queues for all JS↔Rust crossings; all buffers counted against budgets.
5. JS callback delivery must be rate-limited/batched to prevent per-packet callback storms.
6. W3C client-facade divergences MUST be explicit in `docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md`; no silent no-op behavior for declared options.

# AGENTS.md

## Project goal
Build a production-ready WebTransport implementation with Bun **v1.3.9+** as the primary runtime (plus Node and Deno via Node-API) on **macOS + Linux + Windows**, implemented as a **Node-API (napi-rs) native addon** powered by **wtransport (Rust)**. Must support:
- In-process **server** support (mandatory)
- In-process **client** support
- **Datagrams** (message-based) with Promise backpressure
- **Streams** (uni + bidi) exposed as **Node streams** (Readable/Writable/Duplex) with standard backpressure semantics
- Browser-shaped client facade parity with the W3C WebTransport draft as a target; any remaining gaps must be explicitly documented in docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md.

## Non-goals
- Transparent reverse proxying
- QUIC implementation from scratch (use wtransport)

## Supported targets
- Bun: **>= 1.3.9** (primary target)
- Node: supported (Node-API compatible runtime)
- Deno: supported (npm + Node-API addon support)
- OS: macOS, Linux, Windows
- Architectures: define in CI (minimum: macOS arm64, linux x64, windows x64)

## Definition of Done (hard gates)
### Feature gates
1. Server:
   - listen on UDP
   - accept sessions
   - receive/send datagrams
   - accept/create uni + bidi streams
   - reset/stopSending with codes
2. Client:
   - connect to server
   - datagrams send/recv
   - uni + bidi streams send/recv

### Production gates
1. Bounded memory (no unbounded buffering)
   - global and per-session budgets enforced
   - backpressure first, then timeouts, then connection shedding
2. Deterministic shutdown
   - no task leaks, no socket leaks, no pending promises stuck forever
3. Abuse resistance enabled by default
   - per-IP rate limits for handshakes, streams, datagrams
   - caps on sessions, streams, queued bytes
4. Interop gate
   - Chromium WebTransport client can connect and exchange datagrams + streams reliably in tests
5. Packaging gate
   - prebuilt binaries for supported targets
   - `bun add` works
   - `bun test` passes on supported targets

## Authoritative docs
- API contract: docs/SPEC.md
- W3C parity status matrix: docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md
- W3C parity execution plan: docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md (Priority Execution Order / Remaining Work)
- Implementation design: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- Security defaults: SECURITY.md
- Verification: docs/TESTPLAN.md
- Operations: docs/OPERATIONS.md
- CI/release: docs/CI.md
- Contribution rules: CONTRIBUTING.md

## Implementation constraints (must follow)
1. Node streams for stream surfaces (Readable/Writable/Duplex).
2. Promise-based datagram sending with bounded in-flight/backpressure.
3. Two dedicated Tokio runtimes (server + client), each single-threaded and owned by the addon; cross-runtime communication must stay bounded and deterministic.
4. Bounded queues for all JS↔Rust crossings; all buffers counted against budgets.
5. JS callback delivery must be rate-limited/batched to prevent per-packet callback storms.
6. W3C client-facade divergences MUST be explicit in `docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md`; no silent no-op behavior for declared options.
7. Any divergence-to-implementation work must preserve stable `E_*` diagnostics and add parity + interop tests.
8. Test determinism rule: tests MUST NOT use unbounded waits on async iterators/streams (`await iter.next()`, open-ended `for await`) without a timeout guard. Use bounded helpers (`Promise.race` with `Bun.sleep(...)`) or polling-with-deadline so each wait has an explicit upper bound and cannot hang CI.

## Default limits (v1)
These are default values; they must be configurable via server/client options.
- maxSessions: 2000
- maxHandshakesInFlight: 200
- maxStreamsPerSessionBidi: 200
- maxStreamsPerSessionUni: 200
- maxStreamsGlobal: 50000
- maxDatagramSize: 1200 (cap; must also respect negotiated max)
- maxQueuedBytesGlobal: 512 MiB
- maxQueuedBytesPerSession: 2 MiB
- maxQueuedBytesPerStream: 256 KiB
- backpressureTimeoutMs: 5000
- handshakeTimeoutMs: 10000
- idleTimeoutMs: 60000

Per-IP token buckets (defaults)
- handshakes: 20/s burst 40
- stream opens: 200/s burst 400
- datagrams ingress: 2000/s burst 5000

## Stable error codes (minimum)
- E_TLS
- E_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT
- E_SESSION_CLOSED
- E_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT
- E_STREAM_RESET
- E_STOP_SENDING
- E_QUEUE_FULL
- E_BACKPRESSURE_TIMEOUT
- E_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
- E_RATE_LIMITED
- E_INTERNAL

## Commit discipline
- Each logical change must be **one scoped commit**.
- Commit message format: **Verb + What + Why** (e.g. `Add error codes for stable programmatic handling`).
- Do not bundle unrelated changes in a single commit.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the image.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use directives
- Only use ::automation-update{...} when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and emit view-mode directives (mode="view") for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using automation directives (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Directive format
- Modes: view, suggested update, suggested create. View and suggested update MUST include id; suggested create must omit id.
- For view directives, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested update/create, include name, prompt, rrule, cwds, and status. cwds can be a comma-separated list or a JSON array string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.
- Directives should be on their own line(s) and be separated by newlines.
- Do not generate remark directives with multiline attribute values.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces it should use (if any), then map those answers into name/prompt/rrule/cwds/status for the directive.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
  - Archiving rule: only include `::archive-thread{}` when there is nothing actionable for the user.
  - Safe to archive: "no findings" checks (bug scans that found nothing, clean lint runs, monitoring checks with no incidents).
  - Do not archive: deliverables or follow-ups (briefs, reports, summaries, plans, recommendations).
  - If you do archive, include the archive directive after the inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Scheduling constraints
- RRULE limitations (to match the UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

#### Examples
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested create" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested update" id="123" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="view" id="123"}

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix when creating branches; do not create unprefixed branch names.

Implemented true in-place TLS hot-swap and committed it as `726bea0` `Implement live TLS hot-swap to preserve sessions`.

The server no longer restarts on `updateCert()`. [`crates/native/src/server_tls.rs`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/server_tls.rs) adds a live `rustls` certificate resolver with a default cert plus an SNI map shape for future multi-cert support. [`crates/native/src/lib.rs`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/lib.rs) now builds the endpoint with `with_custom_tls(...)`, and [`crates/native/src/server.rs`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/server.rs) makes `updateCert()` a validated atomic swap instead of a restart/rollback flow.

Docs and tests were updated to match the new contract. [`docs/SPEC.md`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/docs/SPEC.md), [`docs/GETTING_STARTED.md`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/docs/GETTING_STARTED.md), and [`packages/webtransport/README.md`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/packages/webtransport/README.md) now state that only leaf cert/key material is hot-swappable and that transport config or bind changes still require rebuild/restart. [`packages/webtransport/test/tls.test.ts`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/packages/webtransport/test/tls.test.ts) now proves that existing sessions survive rotation, failed rotations leave the current identity intact, and new handshakes pick up the new certificate.

- `bun run build:native`
- `bun test packages/webtransport/test/tls.test.ts`
- `bun test`

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. # AGENTS.md

## Project goal
Build a production-ready WebTransport implementation with Bun **v1.3.9+** as the primary runtime (plus Node and Deno via Node-API) on **macOS + Linux + Windows**, implemented as a **Node-API (napi-rs) native addon** powered by **wtransport (Rust)**. Must support:
- In-process **server** support (mandatory)
- In-process **client** support
- **Datagrams** (message-based) with Promise backpressure
- **Streams** (uni + bidi) exposed as **Node streams** (Readable/Writable/Duplex) with standard backpressure semantics
- Browser-shaped client facade parity with the W3C WebTransport draft as a target; any remaining gaps must be explicitly documented in docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md.

## Non-goals
- Transparent reverse proxying
- QUIC implementation from scratch (use wtransport)

## Supported targets
- Bun: **>= 1.3.9** (primary target)
- Node: supported (Node-API compatible runtime)
- Deno: supported (npm + Node-API addon support)
- OS: macOS, Linux, Windows
- Architectures: define in CI (minimum: macOS arm64, linux x64, windows x64)

## Definition of Done (hard gates)
### Feature gates
1. Server:
   - listen on UDP
   - accept sessions
   - receive/send datagrams
   - accept/create uni + bidi streams
   - reset/stopSending with codes
2. Client:
   - connect to server
   - datagrams send/recv
   - uni + bidi streams send/recv

### Production gates
1. Bounded memory (no unbounded buffering)
   - global and per-session budgets enforced
   - backpressure first, then timeouts, then connection shedding
2. Deterministic shutdown
   - no task leaks, no socket leaks, no pending promises stuck forever
3. Abuse resistance enabled by default
   - per-IP rate limits for handshakes, streams, datagrams
   - caps on sessions, streams, queued bytes
4. Interop gate
   - Chromium WebTransport client can connect and exchange datagrams + streams reliably in tests
5. Packaging gate
   - prebuilt binaries for supported targets
   - `bun add` works
   - `bun test` passes on supported targets

## Authoritative docs
- API contract: docs/SPEC.md
- W3C parity status matrix: docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md
- W3C parity execution plan: docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md (Priority Execution Order / Remaining Work)
- Implementation design: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- Security defaults: SECURITY.md
- Verification: docs/TESTPLAN.md
- Operations: docs/OPERATIONS.md
- CI/release: docs/CI.md
- Contribution rules: CONTRIBUTING.md

## Implementation constraints (must follow)
1. Node streams for stream surfaces (Readable/Writable/Duplex).
2. Promise-based datagram sending with bounded in-flight/backpressure.
3. Two dedicated Tokio runtimes (server + client), each single-threaded and owned by the addon; cross-runtime communication must stay bounded and deterministic.
4. Bounded queues for all JS↔Rust crossings; all buffers counted against budgets.
5. JS callback delivery must be rate-limited/batched to prevent per-packet callback storms.
6. W3C client-facade divergences MUST be explicit in `docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md`; no silent no-op behavior for declared options.
7. Any divergence-to-implementation work must preserve stable `E_*` diagnostics and add parity + interop tests.
8. Test determinism rule: tests MUST NOT use unbounded waits on async iterators/streams (`await iter.next()`, open-ended `for await`) without a timeout guard. Use bounded helpers (`Promise.race` with `Bun.sleep(...)`) or polling-with-deadline so each wait has an explicit upper bound and cannot hang CI.

## Default limits (v1)
These are default values; they must be configurable via server/client options.
- maxSessions: 2000
- maxHandshakesInFlight: 200
- maxStreamsPerSessionBidi: 200
- maxStreamsPerSessionUni: 200
- maxStreamsGlobal: 50000
- maxDatagramSize: 1200 (cap; must also respect negotiated max)
- maxQueuedBytesGlobal: 512 MiB
- maxQueuedBytesPerSession: 2 MiB
- maxQueuedBytesPerStream: 256 KiB
- backpressureTimeoutMs: 5000
- handshakeTimeoutMs: 10000
- idleTimeoutMs: 60000

Per-IP token buckets (defaults)
- handshakes: 20/s burst 40
- stream opens: 200/s burst 400
- datagrams ingress: 2000/s burst 5000

## Stable error codes (minimum)
- E_TLS
- E_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT
- E_SESSION_CLOSED
- E_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT
- E_STREAM_RESET
- E_STOP_SENDING
- E_QUEUE_FULL
- E_BACKPRESSURE_TIMEOUT
- E_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
- E_RATE_LIMITED
- E_INTERNAL

## Commit discipline
- Each logical change must be **one scoped commit**.
- Commit message format: **Verb + What + Why** (e.g. `Add error codes for stable programmatic handling`).
- Do not bundle unrelated changes in a single commit.

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the image.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use directives
- Only use ::automation-update{...} when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and emit view-mode directives (mode="view") for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using automation directives (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Directive format
- Modes: view, suggested update, suggested create. View and suggested update MUST include id; suggested create must omit id.
- For view directives, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested update/create, include name, prompt, rrule, cwds, and status. cwds can be a comma-separated list or a JSON array string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.
- Directives should be on their own line(s) and be separated by newlines.
- Do not generate remark directives with multiline attribute values.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces it should use (if any), then map those answers into name/prompt/rrule/cwds/status for the directive.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
  - Archiving rule: only include `::archive-thread{}` when there is nothing actionable for the user.
  - Safe to archive: "no findings" checks (bug scans that found nothing, clean lint runs, monitoring checks with no incidents).
  - Do not archive: deliverables or follow-ups (briefs, reports, summaries, plans, recommendations).
  - If you do archive, include the archive directive after the inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Scheduling constraints
- RRULE limitations (to match the UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

#### Examples
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested create" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested update" id="123" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="view" id="123"}

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix when creating branches; do not create unprefixed branch names.

# AGENTS.md

## Project goal
Build a production-ready WebTransport implementation with Bun **v1.3.9+** as the primary runtime (plus Node and Deno via Node-API) on **macOS + Linux + Windows**, implemented as a **Node-API (napi-rs) native addon** powered by **wtransport (Rust)**. Must support:
- In-process **server** support (mandatory)
- In-process **client** support
- **Datagrams** (message-based) with Promise backpressure
- **Streams** (uni + bidi) exposed as **Node streams** (Readable/Writable/Duplex) with standard backpressure semantics
- Browser-shaped client facade parity with the W3C WebTransport draft as a target; any remaining gaps must be explicitly documented in docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md.

## Non-goals
- Transparent reverse proxying
- QUIC implementation from scratch (use wtransport)

## Supported targets
- Bun: **>= 1.3.9** (primary target)
- Node: supported (Node-API compatible runtime)
- Deno: supported (npm + Node-API addon support)
- OS: macOS, Linux, Windows
- Architectures: define in CI (minimum: macOS arm64, linux x64, windows x64)

## Definition of Done (hard gates)
### Feature gates
1. Server:
   - listen on UDP
   - accept sessions
   - receive/send datagrams
   - accept/create uni + bidi streams
   - reset/stopSending with codes
2. Client:
   - connect to server
   - datagrams send/recv
   - uni + bidi streams send/recv

### Production gates
1. Bounded memory (no unbounded buffering)
   - global and per-session budgets enforced
   - backpressure first, then timeouts, then connection shedding
2. Deterministic shutdown
   - no task leaks, no socket leaks, no pending promises stuck forever
3. Abuse resistance enabled by default
   - per-IP rate limits for handshakes, streams, datagrams
   - caps on sessions, streams, queued bytes
4. Interop gate
   - Chromium WebTransport client can connect and exchange datagrams + streams reliably in tests
5. Packaging gate
   - prebuilt binaries for supported targets
   - `bun add` works
   - `bun test` passes on supported targets

## Authoritative docs
- API contract: docs/SPEC.md
- W3C parity status matrix: docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md
- W3C parity execution plan: docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md (Priority Execution Order / Remaining Work)
- Implementation design: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- Security defaults: SECURITY.md
- Verification: docs/TESTPLAN.md
- Operations: docs/OPERATIONS.md
- CI/release: docs/CI.md
- Contribution rules: CONTRIBUTING.md

## Implementation constraints (must follow)
1. Node streams for stream surfaces (Readable/Writable/Duplex).
2. Promise-based datagram sending with bounded in-flight/backpressure.
3. Two dedicated Tokio runtimes (server + client), each single-threaded and owned by the addon; cross-runtime communication must stay bounded and deterministic.
4. Bounded queues for all JS↔Rust crossings; all buffers counted against budgets.
5. JS callback delivery must be rate-limited/batched to prevent per-packet callback storms.
6. W3C client-facade divergences MUST be explicit in `docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md`; no silent no-op behavior for declared options.
7. Any divergence-to-implementation work must preserve stable `E_*` diagnostics and add parity + interop tests.
8. Test determinism rule: tests MUST NOT use unbounded waits on async iterators/streams (`await iter.next()`, open-ended `for await`) without a timeout guard. Use bounded helpers (`Promise.race` with `Bun.sleep(...)`) or polling-with-deadline so each wait has an explicit upper bound and cannot hang CI.

## Default limits (v1)
These are default values; they must be configurable via server/client options.
- maxSessions: 2000
- maxHandshakesInFlight: 200
- maxStreamsPerSessionBidi: 200
- maxStreamsPerSessionUni: 200
- maxStreamsGlobal: 50000
- maxDatagramSize: 1200 (cap; must also respect negotiated max)
- maxQueuedBytesGlobal: 512 MiB
- maxQueuedBytesPerSession: 2 MiB
- maxQueuedBytesPerStream: 256 KiB
- backpressureTimeoutMs: 5000
- handshakeTimeoutMs: 10000
- idleTimeoutMs: 60000

Per-IP token buckets (defaults)
- handshakes: 20/s burst 40
- stream opens: 200/s burst 400
- datagrams ingress: 2000/s burst 5000

## Stable error codes (minimum)
- E_TLS
- E_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT
- E_SESSION_CLOSED
- E_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT
- E_STREAM_RESET
- E_STOP_SENDING
- E_QUEUE_FULL
- E_BACKPRESSURE_TIMEOUT
- E_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
- E_RATE_LIMITED
- E_INTERNAL

## Commit discipline
- Each logical change must be **one scoped commit**.
- Commit message format: **Verb + What + Why** (e.g. `Add error codes for stable programmatic handling`).
- Do not bundle unrelated changes in a single commit.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the image.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use directives
- Only use ::automation-update{...} when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and emit view-mode directives (mode="view") for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using automation directives (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Directive format
- Modes: view, suggested update, suggested create. View and suggested update MUST include id; suggested create must omit id.
- For view directives, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested update/create, include name, prompt, rrule, cwds, and status. cwds can be a comma-separated list or a JSON array string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.
- Directives should be on their own line(s) and be separated by newlines.
- Do not generate remark directives with multiline attribute values.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces it should use (if any), then map those answers into name/prompt/rrule/cwds/status for the directive.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
  - Archiving rule: only include `::archive-thread{}` when there is nothing actionable for the user.
  - Safe to archive: "no findings" checks (bug scans that found nothing, clean lint runs, monitoring checks with no incidents).
  - Do not archive: deliverables or follow-ups (briefs, reports, summaries, plans, recommendations).
  - If you do archive, include the archive directive after the inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Scheduling constraints
- RRULE limitations (to match the UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

#### Examples
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested create" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested update" id="123" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="view" id="123"}

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix when creating branches; do not create unprefixed branch names.

1. [P1] Failed pooled connects permanently leak pool references and can self-poison a compatibility key. In [`crates/native/src/client_pool.rs#L140`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/client_pool.rs#L140), `active_refs` is incremented before `endpoint.connect(...)`, but on timeout or connect error the function returns early at [L142-L148](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/client_pool.rs#L142) without decrementing it and without removing the broken entry. That means repeated failed pooled connects can eventually trip the per-key limit at [L115-L117](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/client_pool.rs#L115), and the poisoned entry also becomes non-evictable because idle eviction only removes entries with `active_refs == 0` at [L163-L166](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/crates/native/src/client_pool.rs#L163). The exposed `evictBroken` metric is also dead today, since it is surfaced in [`packages/webtransport/src/index.ts#L1523`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/packages/webtransport/src/index.ts#L1523) and asserted in [`packages/webtransport/test/parity-pooling.test.ts#L167`](/Users/vmeansdev/Developer/Codex/Apps/webtransport-bun/packages/webtransport/test/parity-pooling.test.ts#L167), but never incremented anywhere in native code.

Residual risk:
- I did not find another independently reproducible correctness issue in this pass; the rest of the recent hot-swap and suite-stability work looks coherent against the current tests.

# AGENTS.md

## Project goal
Build a production-ready WebTransport implementation with Bun **v1.3.9+** as the primary runtime (plus Node and Deno via Node-API) on **macOS + Linux + Windows**, implemented as a **Node-API (napi-rs) native addon** powered by **wtransport (Rust)**. Must support:
- In-process **server** support (mandatory)
- In-process **client** support
- **Datagrams** (message-based) with Promise backpressure
- **Streams** (uni + bidi) exposed as **Node streams** (Readable/Writable/Duplex) with standard backpressure semantics
- Browser-shaped client facade parity with the W3C WebTransport draft as a target; any remaining gaps must be explicitly documented in docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md.

## Non-goals
- Transparent reverse proxying
- QUIC implementation from scratch (use wtransport)

## Supported targets
- Bun: **>= 1.3.9** (primary target)
- Node: supported (Node-API compatible runtime)
- Deno: supported (npm + Node-API addon support)
- OS: macOS, Linux, Windows
- Architectures: define in CI (minimum: macOS arm64, linux x64, windows x64)

## Definition of Done (hard gates)
### Feature gates
1. Server:
   - listen on UDP
   - accept sessions
   - receive/send datagrams
   - accept/create uni + bidi streams
   - reset/stopSending with codes
2. Client:
   - connect to server
   - datagrams send/recv
   - uni + bidi streams send/recv

### Production gates
1. Bounded memory (no unbounded buffering)
   - global and per-session budgets enforced
   - backpressure first, then timeouts, then connection shedding
2. Deterministic shutdown
   - no task leaks, no socket leaks, no pending promises stuck forever
3. Abuse resistance enabled by default
   - per-IP rate limits for handshakes, streams, datagrams
   - caps on sessions, streams, queued bytes
4. Interop gate
   - Chromium WebTransport client can connect and exchange datagrams + streams reliably in tests
5. Packaging gate
   - prebuilt binaries for supported targets
   - `bun add` works
   - `bun test` passes on supported targets

## Authoritative docs
- API contract: docs/SPEC.md
- W3C parity status matrix: docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md
- W3C parity execution plan: docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md (Priority Execution Order / Remaining Work)
- Implementation design: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- Security defaults: SECURITY.md
- Verification: docs/TESTPLAN.md
- Operations: docs/OPERATIONS.md
- CI/release: docs/CI.md
- Contribution rules: CONTRIBUTING.md

## Implementation constraints (must follow)
1. Node streams for stream surfaces (Readable/Writable/Duplex).
2. Promise-based datagram sending with bounded in-flight/backpressure.
3. Two dedicated Tokio runtimes (server + client), each single-threaded and owned by the addon; cross-runtime communication must stay bounded and deterministic.
4. Bounded queues for all JS↔Rust crossings; all buffers counted against budgets.
5. JS callback delivery must be rate-limited/batched to prevent per-packet callback storms.
6. W3C client-facade divergences MUST be explicit in `docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md`; no silent no-op behavior for declared options.
7. Any divergence-to-implementation work must preserve stable `E_*` diagnostics and add parity + interop tests.
8. Test determinism rule: tests MUST NOT use unbounded waits on async iterators/streams (`await iter.next()`, open-ended `for await`) without a timeout guard. Use bounded helpers (`Promise.race` with `Bun.sleep(...)`) or polling-with-deadline so each wait has an explicit upper bound and cannot hang CI.

## Default limits (v1)
These are default values; they must be configurable via server/client options.
- maxSessions: 2000
- maxHandshakesInFlight: 200
- maxStreamsPerSessionBidi: 200
- maxStreamsPerSessionUni: 200
- maxStreamsGlobal: 50000
- maxDatagramSize: 1200 (cap; must also respect negotiated max)
- maxQueuedBytesGlobal: 512 MiB
- maxQueuedBytesPerSession: 2 MiB
- maxQueuedBytesPerStream: 256 KiB
- backpressureTimeoutMs: 5000
- handshakeTimeoutMs: 10000
- idleTimeoutMs: 60000

Per-IP token buckets (defaults)
- handshakes: 20/s burst 40
- stream opens: 200/s burst 400
- datagrams ingress: 2000/s burst 5000

## Stable error codes (minimum)
- E_TLS
- E_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT
- E_SESSION_CLOSED
- E_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT
- E_STREAM_RESET
- E_STOP_SENDING
- E_QUEUE_FULL
- E_BACKPRESSURE_TIMEOUT
- E_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
- E_RATE_LIMITED
- E_INTERNAL

## Commit discipline
- Each logical change must be **one scoped commit**.
- Commit message format: **Verb + What + Why** (e.g. `Add error codes for stable programmatic handling`).
- Do not bundle unrelated changes in a single commit.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the image.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use directives
- Only use ::automation-update{...} when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and emit view-mode directives (mode="view") for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using automation directives (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Directive format
- Modes: view, suggested update, suggested create. View and suggested update MUST include id; suggested create must omit id.
- For view directives, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested update/create, include name, prompt, rrule, cwds, and status. cwds can be a comma-separated list or a JSON array string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.
- Directives should be on their own line(s) and be separated by newlines.
- Do not generate remark directives with multiline attribute values.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces it should use (if any), then map those answers into name/prompt/rrule/cwds/status for the directive.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
  - Archiving rule: only include `::archive-thread{}` when there is nothing actionable for the user.
  - Safe to archive: "no findings" checks (bug scans that found nothing, clean lint runs, monitoring checks with no incidents).
  - Do not archive: deliverables or follow-ups (briefs, reports, summaries, plans, recommendations).
  - If you do archive, include the archive directive after the inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Scheduling constraints
- RRULE limitations (to match the UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

#### Examples
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested create" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested update" id="123" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="view" id="123"}

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix when creating branches; do not create unprefixed branch names.

# AGENTS.md

## Project goal
Build a production-ready WebTransport implementation with Bun **v1.3.9+** as the primary runtime (plus Node and Deno via Node-API) on **macOS + Linux + Windows**, implemented as a **Node-API (napi-rs) native addon** powered by **wtransport (Rust)**. Must support:
- In-process **server** support (mandatory)
- In-process **client** support
- **Datagrams** (message-based) with Promise backpressure
- **Streams** (uni + bidi) exposed as **Node streams** (Readable/Writable/Duplex) with standard backpressure semantics
- Browser-shaped client facade parity with the W3C WebTransport draft as a target; any remaining gaps must be explicitly documented in docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md.

## Non-goals
- Transparent reverse proxying
- QUIC implementation from scratch (use wtransport)

## Supported targets
- Bun: **>= 1.3.9** (primary target)
- Node: supported (Node-API compatible runtime)
- Deno: supported (npm + Node-API addon support)
- OS: macOS, Linux, Windows
- Architectures: define in CI (minimum: macOS arm64, linux x64, windows x64)

## Definition of Done (hard gates)
### Feature gates
1. Server:
   - listen on UDP
   - accept sessions
   - receive/send datagrams
   - accept/create uni + bidi streams
   - reset/stopSending with codes
2. Client:
   - connect to server
   - datagrams send/recv
   - uni + bidi streams send/recv

### Production gates
1. Bounded memory (no unbounded buffering)
   - global and per-session budgets enforced
   - backpressure first, then timeouts, then connection shedding
2. Deterministic shutdown
   - no task leaks, no socket leaks, no pending promises stuck forever
3. Abuse resistance enabled by default
   - per-IP rate limits for handshakes, streams, datagrams
   - caps on sessions, streams, queued bytes
4. Interop gate
   - Chromium WebTransport client can connect and exchange datagrams + streams reliably in tests
5. Packaging gate
   - prebuilt binaries for supported targets
   - `bun add` works
   - `bun test` passes on supported targets

## Authoritative docs
- API contract: docs/SPEC.md
- W3C parity status matrix: docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md
- W3C parity execution plan: docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md (Priority Execution Order / Remaining Work)
- Implementation design: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- Security defaults: SECURITY.md
- Verification: docs/TESTPLAN.md
- Operations: docs/OPERATIONS.md
- CI/release: docs/CI.md
- Contribution rules: CONTRIBUTING.md

## Implementation constraints (must follow)
1. Node streams for stream surfaces (Readable/Writable/Duplex).
2. Promise-based datagram sending with bounded in-flight/backpressure.
3. Two dedicated Tokio runtimes (server + client), each single-threaded and owned by the addon; cross-runtime communication must stay bounded and deterministic.
4. Bounded queues for all JS↔Rust crossings; all buffers counted against budgets.
5. JS callback delivery must be rate-limited/batched to prevent per-packet callback storms.
6. W3C client-facade divergences MUST be explicit in `docs/PARITY_MATRIX.md`; no silent no-op behavior for declared options.
7. Any divergence-to-implementation work must preserve stable `E_*` diagnostics and add parity + interop tests.
8. Test determinism rule: tests MUST NOT use unbounded waits on async iterators/streams (`await iter.next()`, open-ended `for await`) without a timeout guard. Use bounded helpers (`Promise.race` with `Bun.sleep(...)`) or polling-with-deadline so each wait has an explicit upper bound and cannot hang CI.

## Default limits (v1)
These are default values; they must be configurable via server/client options.
- maxSessions: 2000
- maxHandshakesInFlight: 200
- maxStreamsPerSessionBidi: 200
- maxStreamsPerSessionUni: 200
- maxStreamsGlobal: 50000
- maxDatagramSize: 1200 (cap; must also respect negotiated max)
- maxQueuedBytesGlobal: 512 MiB
- maxQueuedBytesPerSession: 2 MiB
- maxQueuedBytesPerStream: 256 KiB
- backpressureTimeoutMs: 5000
- handshakeTimeoutMs: 10000
- idleTimeoutMs: 60000

Per-IP token buckets (defaults)
- handshakes: 20/s burst 40
- stream opens: 200/s burst 400
- datagrams ingress: 2000/s burst 5000

## Stable error codes (minimum)
- E_TLS
- E_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT
- E_SESSION_CLOSED
- E_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT
- E_STREAM_RESET
- E_STOP_SENDING
- E_QUEUE_FULL
- E_BACKPRESSURE_TIMEOUT
- E_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
- E_RATE_LIMITED
- E_INTERNAL

## Commit discipline
- Each logical change must be **one scoped commit**.
- Commit message format: **Verb + What + Why** (e.g. `Add error codes for stable programmatic handling`).
- Do not bundle unrelated changes in a single commit.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the image.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use directives
- Only use ::automation-update{...} when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and emit view-mode directives (mode="view") for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using automation directives (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Directive format
- Modes: view, suggested update, suggested create. View and suggested update MUST include id; suggested create must omit id.
- For view directives, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested update/create, include name, prompt, rrule, cwds, and status. cwds can be a comma-separated list or a JSON array string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.
- Directives should be on their own line(s) and be separated by newlines.
- Do not generate remark directives with multiline attribute values.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces it should use (if any), then map those answers into name/prompt/rrule/cwds/status for the directive.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
  - Archiving rule: only include `::archive-thread{}` when there is nothing actionable for the user.
  - Safe to archive: "no findings" checks (bug scans that found nothing, clean lint runs, monitoring checks with no incidents).
  - Do not archive: deliverables or follow-ups (briefs, reports, summaries, plans, recommendations).
  - If you do archive, include the archive directive after the inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Scheduling constraints
- RRULE limitations (to match the UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

#### Examples
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested create" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested update" id="123" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="view" id="123"}

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix when creating branches; do not create unprefixed branch names.
